audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart read "Skill" on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet chart both read Lux/Lux/Lux/Lux/Skill/Skill/Swain — the page rendered two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: Lux Q is 1175 range and E 1100; Swain's Death's Hand is 750 and Nevermove 850, so the early rows are genuinely Lux's. Late, Demonic Ascension (120s) plus Nevermove chaining flips it to Swain, matching the content layer.
audit.corrected: Full phases[0..3].side set to Lux, phases[6].side to Swain, ratings and whys rewritten to match. win[N] already held these sides, so no content-layer chart edits were needed (a no-op edit would have taken the group down).

audit.why: Spike structure is sound: Lost Chapter chip, level 6 Final Spark (60/50/40s), Luden's deletion, and Swain's scaling off Ravenous Flock stacks. spikes[] has all four entries.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text grounded with the actual sustain mechanic and the Grievous Wounds requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Nevermove roots on its RETURN pass, not the outgoing throw, and it is Swain's only lockdown on a 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s cooldown. breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all, and Demonic Ascension's real 120s cooldown was replaced by a fabricated "fifteen-second invitation".
audit.why: Riot's own E text: "launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits." That timing is the whole spacing rule for an immobile mage, and 120s vs Lux's 60s R is the actual window maths.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field now names 120s Ascension, 12s Nevermove and 10s Q; dos/donts rewritten around the return-pass root and real timers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned only in report[8]; the spike text told you to out-poke a champion who heals off Soul Fragments.
audit.why: missingInteractions: needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated both fire on Ravenous Flock.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text and breakdown.carry now name Grievous Wounds explicitly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, and dosFull[0].d described Demonic Ascension under an E-poke title.
audit.why: Lint findings COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2 plus the same defect in dosFull[0].d; body did not match the promised title.
audit.corrected: All three bodies rewritten to match their titles at the same length.

audit.whatIsWrong: lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED: the body was the tradeGood string verbatim under an unrelated title.
audit.why: An earlier proposal targeted these same fields but its replacement text overshot the +/-10% length rule, so apply-proposals dropped the edit and the defect survived on disk.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the same meaning inside the length budget, grounded in real ability names and cooldowns from champ-data/_kits: dosFull[1].d.

edits.after: E-poke from max range on his last-hits: 1100 beats his 750 Death's Hand, so the chip and passive auto are free.

edits.after: Q joins: at 1175 you out-range everything but his W, so his step-ups cost him.

edits.after: Full kit: Q-E-auto chunks him, and Nevermove only roots on the return — walk through it.

edits.after: Lux

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact. Bank Manaflow and hold Q for his aggression, not yours.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact and deny Soul Fragments; hold Q for his 12s Nevermove.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Swain

edits.before: Late Lux decides fights from a screen away: root the entry, slow the pit, and laser the clump your team froze.
edits.after: Late, his Demonic Ascension drains a whole clump while Nevermove chains you — you get one laser, he gets a fight.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Prismatic Barrier has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Demonic Ascension: 120s, the longest cooldown in the lane — when it drops, the next two minutes belong to you. - Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 and roots on the return pass, not the throw. - Your Q is 10s: bank it for his step-up, never for poke.

edits.before: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Death's Hand is 750 range and needs him close; E at 1100 lands on the minion he wants, so he eats it or drops the CS.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Every damaging spell charges Illumination — land E, then auto to ignite it from outside 850 units, where Nevermove cannot answer.

edits.before: Swain burns Demonic Ascension on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: If Nevermove misses he is CC-less for 12 seconds — that is when your Q lands.

edits.before: That’s Swain’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Q is your root, not poke — miss it and his 12s Nevermove has a free target.

edits.before: Your W answers exactly one combo per fight — shield the spell that kills, not the one that stings.
edits.after: E is 10s at rank 1; without it you farm inside Death's Hand range and feed his Soul Fragment healing.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 and it is your only screen-range answer to his Ascension commit — spend it on him, not a caster wave.

edits.before: Swain wins by landing Demonic Ascension, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Swain wins by rooting you on Nevermove's return, dragging you into Demonic Ascension, and healing back all the poke.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by killing him before Ascension: Q root, E detonate, Final Spark — and buy Grievous Wounds so his Soul Fragments cannot undo the work.

edits.before: Swain's sustain scales with HP and AP; once he has an item he heals through your poke inside his R. Keep trades short and never stand in his soul-drain radius, or you feed his passive stacks.
edits.after: Swain's sustain scales with HP and AP — Soul Fragments heal him and permanently raise his max health, so out-poking him needs Grievous Wounds, not more damage. Keep trades short and deny fragments.

notes: Full-layer chart was blanket 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] matched the packet; fixed the full layer to agree, no win[N] edits needed (they were already correct — a no-op would have failed the group). Ravenous Flock's exact heal/max-health numbers are not in the kit text, so the anti-heal advice is stated qualitatively. breakdown.wave, ahead and breakdown.feeding read as templated but the enemy-specific replacement would not fit the ±10% band without dropping real content, so they were left alone. QA re-scope: previous edits to dosFull[1].d were rejected for length drift; re-proposed within budget. Cooldowns quoted are Riot per-rank values from the kit files; no spell-shield, cleanse or minion-block behaviour is asserted anywhere, since the kits do not state it.
